meta.name: Sourdough Discard Cheese Crackers

source.name: Research Synthesis (12 sources)
source.author: Primary influences: Wild Thistle Kitchen, King Arthur Baking, Natasha's Kitchen

meta.total_time: ~1.5 hrs (30 min active, 30 min chill, 20 min bake)
meta.description: Sharp cheddar crackers with sourdough tang, smoked paprika, and black pepper. Uses unfed sourdough discard as the base — no waste, maximum flavor. Roll thin and dock well for snappy, Cheez-It-adjacent results.

change_log.summary: Backfill config.stats (PF-264): new group 'Crackers & Snacks', defaultYield 90 crackers (midpoint of yields ~80-100), servingsPerItem 1. Enables throughput modeling + per-cracker price rollups.

states.title: Grate Cheese
states.direction: Using the fine holes of a box grater, grate the block of sharp cheddar. Set aside.
states.exit_condition: 170g cheese finely grated with no large chunks remaining

notes.text: Block cheese only — pre-shredded cheese contains anti-caking agents (cellulose, potato starch) that prevent proper melting and integration into the dough.

states.title: Whisk Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In the stand mixer bowl, whisk together flour, fine salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly combined with uniform spice color throughout

states.title: Cut in Butter
states.direction: Add softened butter to dry ingredients. Using the paddle attachment on low speed, mix until butter is incorporated and mixture resembles coarse crumbs, about 1 minute.
states.exit_condition: Butter fully incorporated; mixture has a sandy, coarse crumb texture

states.title: Add Discard & Cheese
states.direction: Add sourdough discard and grated cheddar to the bowl. Paddle on low speed until dough just comes together into a cohesive mass, about 1-2 minutes. Do not overmix.
states.exit_condition: Dough is cohesive and holds together when pressed; no loose flour remaining

notes.text: Use flat/unfed discard, not active bubbly starter. Active starter causes puffing during baking, working against the flat, crispy cracker texture you want.

states.title: Chill Dough
states.direction: Shape dough into a flat disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes minimum (up to 2 days).
states.exit_condition: Dough is firm and cold, easy to handle without sticking

notes.text: Flattening into a disc before chilling speeds up cooling and makes rolling easier.

states.title: Roll Dough Ultra-Thin
states.direction: Place dough between two sheets of parchment paper. Roll to 0.16cm thickness — as thin as possible without tearing. Work from center outward, rotating 90° periodically for even thickness.
states.exit_condition: Dough is uniformly 0.16cm thick with no visibly thicker areas

notes.text: Rolling thin enough is the #1 factor separating great crackers from mediocre ones. If you can't hit 0.16cm, go as thin as you can — thinner is always better for crispness.
If dough becomes too soft and sticky while rolling, return to fridge for 10 minutes, then continue.

states.title: Cut Squares
states.direction: Using a pizza cutter or sharp knife, cut the rolled dough into 2.5cm squares. No need to separate — they break apart after baking. Transfer parchment with cut dough to a baking sheet.
states.exit_condition: Dough cut into uniform 2.5cm grid on parchment-lined baking sheet

states.title: Dock & Salt
states.direction: Using a fork or toothpick, poke a hole in the center of each cracker square. Sprinkle flaky salt evenly over the tops.
states.exit_condition: Every cracker has at least one dock hole; flaky salt visible on surface

notes.text: Docking prevents steam puffing during baking. Without it, crackers puff unevenly.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Position rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat to 350°F (175°C).

states.title: Bake Crackers
states.direction: Bake for 15-20 minutes, rotating the sheet halfway through. Watch closely after 12 minutes — edges brown fast.
states.exit_condition: Crackers are golden brown at the edges; center crackers have deepened in color but are not dark brown

notes.text: Pull slightly early if in doubt — crackers continue to crisp as they cool. Overbaked crackers taste bitter from burnt cheese.

reminders.prompt: Record bake time and color at edges

states.title: Cool Completely
states.direction: Leave crackers on the baking sheet to cool completely, at least 15 minutes. They crisp significantly as they cool.
states.exit_condition: Crackers are room temperature and snap cleanly when broken — no bend or flex

notes.text: Do not transfer to a container until fully cooled. Trapped steam from warm crackers creates sogginess.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 5-7 days. Glass container extends shelf life.

methods.detail: 300°F (150°C) for 3-5 minutes to re-crisp if softened. Cool on pan before eating.

techniques.name: Ultra-thin rolling (0.16cm)
techniques.rationale: Universal consensus. #1 factor for crispy crackers.

techniques.name: Full docking
techniques.rationale: Prevents steam puffing. Fork holes or toothpick center hole per cracker.

techniques.name: Block cheese, hand-grated
techniques.rationale: Pre-shredded has anti-caking agents that prevent proper melting.

techniques.name: Cut before baking
techniques.rationale: Pizza cutter for clean squares. Pre-cutting is simpler than mid-bake scoring.

techniques.name: Cool completely on pan
techniques.rationale: Crackers crisp as they cool. Moving early or storing warm = soggy.

techniques.name: Stand mixer paddle on low
techniques.rationale: Low speed avoids overworking gluten. Food processor also works.
